limitations: Busy percentages and loop delay are current process samples, not full incident measurements or player ping.
Death latency retains the last 128 completed samples; recentSlow is bounded by count. Visible channel-1 slow events start at 15:45:24 Turkey time, after the 15:43 recovery message.

The displayed diagnostics omit coordinator queue/terminal wait stages. Internal stage timing is opt-in via CORE511_STAGE_TIMING=1, defaults disabled, and records completed waits only; the live flag is unknown.
These screenshots do not prove a network fault, a fixed nine-minute timeout, a CPU-capacity problem, or the cause of the admission stall.

journalScreenshots.transcription: Selected clearly visible records only; full journal not available.

followingErrors.scope: Different boot-local actor references; recurring 10-second session refresh. Screenshot ends before the 40-second disconnected retirement boundary.

interpretation: The unknown-command watcher triggered global recovery twice. Its underlying original writer exception is not visible in these screenshots.
The global_world_busy stack is a recovery-in-progress fence in SharedCombatBridge.terminalIdle called from CoreCoordinator.serial. It is not proof of the first trigger.
RecoveryCause fills attack/sourceChannel/phase from an active terminal when no explicit context exists; these fields alone do not prove the attack threw the first error.
The retained first simulation ticks around12:33:56Z belong to the replacement generation after this recovery.
The client eight-second timeout mismatch and recovery-finalization race are separately reproduced source defects, not yet proven to explain the full reported interval.
